steps.title: Meet the ReLU assessment
steps.text:
A layer can combine inputs with weights and offsets, but models also need ways to change how values pass through. An activation is one such transformation. ReLU keeps a number when it is positive and replaces it with zero when it is negative. Zero stays zero.

This simple gate is common in neural networks. Here you will build and check the transformation itself, so you can see exactly which values it changes. This assessment does not train a classifier or turn scores into probabilities.

The supplied canvas starts with two unconnected blocks:
- Input receives rows with two numeric features. The checker supplies the actual numbers.
- Result must receive two features in the same order, with ReLU applied separately to each number.

Add the connecting calculation. This lesson's adapter also requires a Linear block with explicit parameters. That is a requirement of this construction exercise, not a requirement for using ReLU in every model.

steps.title: Build the connected transformation
steps.text:
1. Read the public examples in Task, supplied values & hints. Predict which numbers change and which stay the same.
2. Place the allowed Linear and ReLU components, then connect Input through your construction to Result. ReLU must be on the connected path that reaches the output; an unused block cannot transform the values.
3. Select Linear and use Parameters to set two input features and two output features. Initialize explicit weights and biases if needed. Choose values that preserve the intended ReLU behavior rather than changing the feature order or adding an unwanted shift.
4. ReLU itself has no settings or trainable numbers. Keep each input value independent: one feature's value should not determine how its neighbor is transformed.
5. Finish pending numeric edits before choosing Submit assessment in the rail.

More than one valid construction can pass. The checker compares the resulting transformation, while enforcing this task's required components.

steps.title: Submit and read the result
steps.text:
Choose Submit assessment in Check your construction. The checker supplies independent negative, zero and positive values and compares your output with ReLU.

Read Assessment feedback when checking finishes:
- Negative inputs should become zero.
- Zero and positive inputs should keep their values.
- Preserve both feature positions and the number of rows. Changing a neighboring value must not change this value's result.

If checking cannot start or is cancelled, resolve that condition before treating it as evidence about the transformation. If values are wrong, inspect the surrounding Linear weights and biases as well as the connections.

Completion requires a passing assessment with its receipt saved. After edits, submit again to check the new construction. Saving keeps your attempt; it does not itself establish correctness.

steps.title: The required behavior
steps.text:
Apply ReLU to every input number independently. Replace a negative value with zero; keep zero and positive values unchanged. Return two features per row in their original order.

Include ReLU on the connected path to Result and satisfy the adapter's requirement for an explicitly configured Linear block. Equivalent valid arrangements are accepted.

steps.title: Work on the canvas
steps.text:
Drag allowed components onto the canvas and connect an output port to the next input port. A port is a block's connection point.

Select a Linear block to edit its sizes and numbers in Parameters. Check the complete path from Input to Result before submitting. This Construction uses Submit assessment, not an ordinary training run.

steps.title: Predict these public examples
steps.text:
These are illustrative rows showing the requested rule, not captured results from your construction:

- Input [−2, 0] becomes [0, 0]. The negative value is clipped; zero is unchanged.
- Input [1, 2] stays [1, 2]. Each positive value passes through.

The two columns are separate features. Apply the rule to each cell without swapping columns, combining neighbors or normalizing the row. The assessment uses additional inputs, so the construction must implement the rule rather than return these two fixed rows.

steps.title: Configure the Linear scaffold
steps.text:
This lesson's adapter requires at least one Linear block with explicit weights and biases. ReLU itself has no configurable or trainable parameters.

For a two-feature Linear layer, each weight-table row produces one output feature and each column receives one input feature. Row and column indices begin at 0. Bias adds a fixed offset to each output.

A Linear layer that leaves the values unchanged is a useful scaffold. Reason about which weights preserve each feature and which entries would mix another feature into it. Keep offsets from shifting the point where negative values become zero. You may use an equivalent construction, provided it still performs the required transformation.

steps.title: Reason about independence and repetition
steps.text:
ReLU operates on one number at a time. If one input stays fixed while its neighbor changes, that fixed input's ReLU result stays the same.

Applying ReLU twice gives the same result as applying it once: after the first application, every value is already zero or positive. Repeated ReLU blocks can therefore be valid, provided the rest of the construction preserves the requested behavior.

Assessment feedback reports the checker outcome. It does not expose the private input/output fixtures as a measured-results table.

steps.title: What completion means
steps.text:
The assessment checks the ReLU transformation on independent inputs while preserving rows and feature order. It also requires the declared ReLU component on the connected output path and explicit Linear parameters required by this adapter.

Completion requires a passing Submit assessment result with its receipt saved. Reading the examples or saving an unfinished graph does not establish completion. Existing criteria and resource limits remain available in Optional · exact checks and limits.

steps.title: Optional · understand the curve
steps.text:
ReLU is short for rectified linear unit:

ReLU(x) = max(x, 0)

x is one input number. max chooses the larger of that number and zero. Positive inputs pass through unchanged; negative inputs become zero.

For a positive input, a small increase produces the same increase in output. A negative input remains at zero for small changes that keep it negative. At exactly zero the curve has a corner, without one unique mathematical slope. This runner uses zero as its small-change sensitivity convention there. That convention is optional background, not an additional requirement of this forward-value assessment.

ReLU does not automatically repair unstable training, and its outputs are not probabilities. Its usefulness depends on where it belongs in the model.
